findings.title: A Make public sent before this release to the user's own account now reads as change. A stealth mint, a pool's start or a funding takes it before money made private, while the docs say it goes with that money or after it
findings.scenario:
1. On 1.9.1 the user makes 20 ₳ public to their own account 2. The form offers their own accounts (ownAccounts="private", OwnWarning) and is paid from Bob's 30 ₳ payment R.
2. 1.9.1 seals the change C (about 9.8 ₳) as received:R. The entry keeps only a shortHex detail, nothing that names the account.
3. After the update, the private balance holds C and 50 ₳ made private from account 0 (public:0).
4. classOf runs spendLeft(received:R, W), which gives {change:W+received:R, origin change}: Mint 4 and Fund 4, ahead of Own 5. They also merge in tier 0 before it.
5. A stealth mint, a private pool start or a funding with nothing fresher that pays alone takes C, because step 1 sorts by rank before size.
6. On chain the new Seedelf or session is now tied to account 2 through W, and Bob can tie it to the Seedelf he paid. The docs promise that what a Make public to the account left goes with money made private, or after it.

Where two fixes meet: round two's l2time#2 verifier accepted the case it couldn't tell apart because "change:<tx> ranks after own money anyway". l2rank#6 removed that reason.

This isn't a regression. C ranked Mint 0 on 1.9.1 and Mint 1 at 5447f7e5. Make public to one's own account is that screen's main use, so most old Make-public change in users' balances is this case.
findings.who: Nobody acts; it's upgrade data. It affects any user who sent a Make public to their own account on 1.9.1 or earlier and still holds its change. The link is made by the default pick.
findings.evidence:
histories.ts:187-192 `if (all.some(left)) return merged([kept]); if (all.some((p) => accountIn(p) !== undefined)) return kept; return merged([kept, leftBy(txHash)]);`

activity.ts:800 `LEAVES_CHANGE = new Set(["transfer", "withdraw", "mint", "remove", "lovejoin-launch"])`; :810 `if (stored) return LEAVES_CHANGE.has(entry.kind) ? spendLeft(stored, entry.txHash) : stored;`

At web-wallet/1.9.1: withdraw.ts:147 `origin: changeHistory(seen, p.inputs)` (no tiedBy). activity.ts:350-356 gives the withdraw entry only `several(paid.map((p) => (p.handle ? ... : shortHex(String(p.address)))))`.

build.rs:2512-2513 `Change => 4, Own => 5,` (Mint); :2524-2525 (Fund).

The docs:
- privacy.md:109: "Change that's tied to one of your accounts or private sessions already (what a Make public to the account left, or change of money you made private) goes with that money, or after it."
- architecture.md:151: "...but where that history names a public account, as a Make public's to one of the user's own accounts does (l2time#2)." 1.9.1's never does.
- privacy.md:176, flows.md:134 and keys-and-accounts.md:151 say the Made private (account n) tag marks what a Make public to that account left. An old one is tagged Change, Received.

The tests: r3-change-classes.test.ts pins the 1.9.1 shape as "a Make public to someone else" (change). Its own-account control uses only this release's shape, merged([madePrivate(0), paidByR0]).

round3.json R3-code l2time#2 left: "can't be told apart and reads as change".
findings.fix:
Pick one:
(a) Words only. In privacy.md:109 and :176, flows.md:134 and keys-and-accounts.md:151, say this holds for a Make public sent from this version on. One an earlier version sent kept no record of where it went, so its change reads as change, before money made private, even where it paid your own account. In architecture.md:151, drop "as a Make public's to one of the user's own accounts does".
(b) Code. In spendLeft, or in classOf for kind "withdraw", give a kept-before Make public (no change: part, no public: part) the change:<tx> part but origin "session", so it ranks after Own as round two had it. This is the conservative reading. It costs answer 5's order for an old Make public to a stranger.
(c) Matching the entry's shortHex detail against the known accounts' addresses would be fragile and needs the keys in classOf. Not recommended.

For (b), add a test: a 1.9.1-shaped withdraw entry (received:R0) beside public:0. The stealth mint takes public:0.
findings.owner_question: A Make public an earlier version sent can't say whether it paid your own account. Should its change go before money made private, as change (your fifth answer read literally), or after it, as change tied to an account (the cautious reading)? The docs then need to say which.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 51e66221. I traced it end to end and found no guard the finder missed. But it is narrower than the finding says: the finding's own numbers don't produce a different pick.

1. What 1.9.1 kept. At web-wallet/1.9.1, withdraw.ts:147 seals `origin: changeHistory(seen, p.inputs)`. For a Make public paid from Bob's R, that is {received:R, received}.
- 1.9.1 activity.ts:335 stores `readClass(s.origin)`. activity.ts:355 keeps only `$handle` or `shortHex(String(p.address))` as the entry's detail.
- The form offered the user's own accounts (Withdraw.tsx:315 `ownAccounts="private"`). Nothing in the entry names the account.

2. Nothing rewrites it later. There's no migration. arrived() skips W because it's in `ours` (activity.ts:549, :572), and HEAD's sent() (:403-444) never reads `ownAccount`.

3. How HEAD reads it.
- activity.ts:800 puts "withdraw" in LEAVES_CHANGE, so :810 calls `spendLeft(stored, entry.txHash)`.
- histories.ts:187-192: the kept class has no change: part and no public: part, so it returns `merged([kept, leftBy(txHash)])`.
- originOfAll (:149-154) names that "change".
- classes() (:485-489) keeps it as is: it isn't unknown or received, so the copy check never runs.

4. How selection ranks it.
- lib.rs:2155 maps "change" to Origin::Change. The stealth mint (lib.rs:2614) and the private pool start (:2925) both use Purpose::Mint.
- build.rs:2508-2514 ranks Mint `Change => 4, Own => 5`. :2519-2527 ranks Fund the same.
- Both are tier 0 (:2536-2541).
- Step 1 sorts by (last, rank), then by lovelace (build.rs:2857, one_more :2752). Merging order a sorts by tier, then rank.

5. What the docs claim, which the code doesn't do for this change:
- privacy.md:109: "what a Make public to the account left ... goes with that money, or after it".
- privacy.md:172: the tie is "(a Make public to one of your own accounts, to that account)", and "Change whose history an earlier version kept gets its spend's tie".
- privacy.md:176, flows.md:134 and keys-and-accounts.md:151 say the Made private (account n) tag marks it.
- architecture.md:151 adds "as a Make public's to one of the user's own accounts does", but a history 1.9.1 kept doesn't name the account.
- No doc mentions the residue. round3.json's l2time#2 "left" note names it.

6. The test, on a copy with the round-three WebAssembly package (r3-change-classes.test.ts passes 23/23 there):
- The 1.9.1-shaped change reads {change:W+received:R0, change}, tagged [Change, Received].
- A stealth mint spent W#1 (the old 29.8 ₳ change) instead of A0#0 (10 ₳ made private).
- A funding spent W#1 (49.8 ₳) instead of A0#0 (30 ₳).
- The controls, with this release's shape (public:0+received:R0, own), took A0#0 both times.

7. Where the finding overstates.
- With its own numbers (C 9.8 ₳, 50 ₳ made private), the documented rule ("goes with that money": the same rank) still takes the smaller C. The pin shows both shapes spend W#1.
- The pick differs only where money made private that pays alone is smaller than C, or in merge order. Then the new Seedelf is tied to account n and to R's payer, rather than to account 0. Both are ties to a public account, so the privacy-link side is weak.
- "Most old Make-public change" is too wide. 1.9.1's Pay order took Own money first, and change of that names public:n, which spendLeft keeps.
- It isn't a regression. C ranked Mint 0 on 1.9.1, Mint 1 at 5447f7e5 and Mint 4 now.

8. Where two fixes meet. l2time#2's verifier accepted this case because "change:<tx> ranks after own money anyway" (review2.json). l2rank#6 then put Change at 4, ahead of Own at 5.

Why medium: the rubric counts a claim wider than the code as medium.

Which of these to take is the owner's question as the finding words it. (a) is enough to make the docs true either way.

(a) Words only. No code change, and no policy entry, since nothing sent, kept or revealed changes.

- privacy.md:172, after "...but where that history names one of your accounts.": "A Make public an earlier version sent to one of your own accounts didn't note the account, so its change carries that payment's tie, as change."

- architecture.md:151: after "as a Make public's to one of the user's own accounts does" add "from this release on (`tiedBy`); 1.9.1's kept no account, so its change reads `change:<tx>` and ranks before money made private (l3rank#1)".
- Add a pin to tests/r3-change-classes.test.ts: spent(t, "withdraw", W, receivedIn(R0), {payments:[{address: <own receive_0>, ...}]}) reads {change:W+received:R0, change}, tagged [Change, Received].

(b) Code. In classOf/spendLeft, for kind "withdraw" with no change: part and no public: part, keep the id merged([kept, leftBy(W)]) but set origin "own" (rank 5, tier 0, as this release's own-account Make public reads) or "session" (rank 6, which Fund puts in tier 1). Caveats:
- merged() (histories.ts:174) and lib.rs merged_class work the origin out again from the parts. Once C is spent or merged, its change reads "change" again. To make it stick you need a marker part: say `withdrew:<tx>`, read by originOf as session and counted in `later`, tagged Change, counted as change by historiesNote, and mirrored in lib.rs origin_of/merged_class.
- An old Make public to a stranger also moves after money made private. r3-change-classes.test.ts:108 then expects own or session.
- The tag stays Change and Received, so the tag lines in (a) are needed anyway.
- With (b), my mint and funding cases pass; drop the test's "Made private" tag assertion.

(c) Match the entry's detail against the accounts' addresses. Its last 6 characters are the bech32 checksum, so where a match exists it's reliable. But a `$handle` detail, or several payees (only the first is kept), can't be matched, and classOf would need to derive keys under withKeys. Not recommended.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. The medium comes from the docs, which round three wrote and which say more than the code does. The code side alone is narrower than the finding says, and its own scenario doesn't show the harm.

What the code does:
- At web-wallet/1.9.1, withdraw.ts:147 kept `origin: changeHistory(seen, p.inputs)`, the inputs' history alone. The entry kept only `several(paid.map((p) => (p.handle ? ... : shortHex(String(p.address)))))` (1.9.1 activity.ts ~350-356). Nothing names the account. `tiedBy` first appears in 9f8df1b1 (round two), so no shipped version wrote it.
- classOf (activity.ts:810) runs `spendLeft(stored, entry.txHash)` for every withdraw entry (LEAVES_CHANGE, :800). spendLeft (histories.ts:187-192) adds leftBy unless the history names a public account.
- I ran a scratch copy of the real histories.ts with i18n stubbed: scratchpad/l3rank1/check.ts.
  - A 1.9.1 own-account Make public paid by R reads {change:W+received:R, origin change}, the same as this release's Make public to a stranger.
  - This release's own-account one reads {public:2+received:R, origin own}.
- Ranks: build.rs:2512-2513 (Mint) and :2524-2525 (Fund) give `Change => 4, Own => 5`.
- Step 1 sorts by rank, then size, smallest first (one_more, build.rs:2752 `(rank(u), lovelace_of(u))`). Both are tier 0.

Where the scenario is wrong: with its numbers (C 9.8 ₳, public:0 50 ₳), the documented rule also takes C. Ranked with money made private, C is still the smallest of rank 5 that pays alone. So "because step 1 sorts by rank before size" isn't what makes the difference there. Same scratch check, Mint and Fund alike:
- C 30 ₳ beside public:0 5 ₳: the code takes C, the documented rule takes public:0. Both tie the new Seedelf to one of the user's accounts (account 2 through W, or account 0 through its move-in), so this is mostly sideways. C also lets Bob tie it to the Seedelf he paid.
- C 9.8 ₳ beside D 20 ₳, an earlier Send's change (change:S+received:X): the code takes C, the documented rule takes D. This is the real loss: an account tie made by default where a tie to a payment to someone else was there.

Not a regression. In every version C ranked before money made private: Mint 0 and Fund 1 at 1.9.1, Mint 1 and Fund 1 at 5447f7e5, 4 and 4 now. Round three moved it later.

Nothing catches it:
- historiesNote says nothing for one class.
- The tags read Change and Received (historyTags), so a user locking by tag won't lock it.
- The fixer did write the limit down (round3.json R3-code l2time#2 left: "can't be told apart and reads as change"). It never reached the docs.

Docs that say more than the code. Each line was last changed by round-three commits (211c65c2, b5c28f1e). Each is unqualified and false for this upgrade data:
- privacy.md:109: what a Make public to the account left "goes with that money, or after it".
- privacy.md:172: "Change whose history an earlier version kept gets its spend's tie". The same bullet says that tie is the account, but the code gives change:W.
- privacy.md:176, flows.md:134, keys-and-accounts.md:151: the Made private (account n) tag "also marks what a Make public to that account left".
- architecture.md:151: "as a Make public's to one of the user's own accounts does". No shipped version's history does that.

No UI string makes this claim, and the privacy policy's 18 November entry is forward-looking.

Who is affected:
- Nobody acts: it's upgrade data.
- Reached by a user who made a Make public to their own account on 1.9.1 or earlier and still holds its change.
- That Make public was paid from received money, a box or Unknown money. One paid from money made private keeps public:n and isn't affected.
- They then make a stealth mint (opt-in), or a pool start or a funding (both private by default), with nothing fresher paying alone.

findings.title: When the private balance pays a box's way back, a box of unknown making (or a plain box) merged with a received payment reads as received: tied with money others paid, and no longer a box to selection. The private payer also now prefers such a box
findings.scenario:
1. Mallory deposits a box under S1's register, copied as found (d = 1), into a token pool whose boxes can't pay their own way back.
2. Bring every box back now sends it with paid: "private" (stuck, :7892).
3. With no box-class UTxO in the private balance, the smallest UTxO pays, here Bob's received R.
4. own = unplacedBox(w), and merged([own, received:R]) gives box:w+received:R+unknown:w. REACH puts received ahead of lovejoin and unknown, so the origin is "received": Mint 1, Fund 1, tier 0.
5. The next stealth mint can take it as the smallest money others paid. The new Seedelf is then tied in the open to S1, which is l2rank#1's harm. A merge no longer keeps it last, one at a time.

Rule 1 says such a way back goes after money others paid and stays a box. REACH has the same mismatch for a plain or unplaced box paid back by Unknown money: it reads lovejoin (Mint 2), ahead of Unknown alone (3).

Where rule 1 meets call 36's payer order: fromLovejoin prefers a payer whose origin is lovejoin or mixed. Mallory's planted way back W is now lovejoin (it was received at 5447f7e5), so it's now the first payer for another stuck box's way back. That merges the user's own box, a mixed one included, with a box tied to S1 in the open.
findings.who: A stranger (a deposit), plus the user bringing it back (Bring every box back now, or Bring one back paid privately) from a stuck token pool while the private balance holds no box.
findings.evidence:
lovejoin.ts:8225 `const besides = [...(spent ? [spent.class] : []), ...(ties ?? []).map(madePrivate)];` and :8230 `origin = spent || !plain ? (besides.length ? merged([own, ...besides]) : own) : undefined;`

histories.ts:140 `const REACH: Origin[] = ["session", "own", "received", "lovejoin", "unknown"];`

build.rs:2509-2510 `Received => 1, Lovejoin => 2`; :2538 `(_, Origin::Lovejoin | Origin::Mixed) => 2` (received is tier 0).

lovejoin.ts:7892 `...(stuck ? { paid: "private" as const } : {}),`; :8132 `const fromLovejoin = (u) => (["lovejoin", "mixed"].includes(classes[outpoint(u)]?.origin ?? "") ? 0 : 1);`

privacy.md:169 has the exception ("but where other money paid the way back"). The policy (privacy-policy.md:93, "any other goes after money others paid you") and architecture.md:152 ("still a box to selection, which `Mint` and `Fund` take after money others paid") don't.

round3.json R3-code l2rank#1 left: "a stuck-pool edge, accepted". That was accepted by the fixer, not decided by the owner.
findings.fix:
In withdrawOne, when `spent` is set and own.origin is lovejoin (boxFrom or unplacedBox), keep the merged class at lovejoin wherever merged() would name it received or unknown, and keep own, session and change as merged gives them:
`const m = merged([own, ...besides]); origin = own.origin === "lovejoin" && ["received", "unknown"].includes(m.origin) ? { ...m, origin: "lovejoin" } : m;` (readClass keeps a stored origin).

In the private payer order, rank a box of unknown making (a class with its box's own unknown:<tx>) after the other boxes.

Or accept it, and copy privacy.md:169's exception into the policy's 18 November entry and architecture.md:152.

Test: unplaced box, stuck pool, a private balance of Bob's 20 ₳ only. The way back's origin must not be received.
findings.owner_question: When your private balance pays a box's way back with a payment you received, should what comes back still go after money others paid and stay a box (rule 1)? Or should it rank as that payment?

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 51e66221, first by reading, then by a Vitest run with the real WebAssembly. The package was built at 00:57, after the last Rust change at 00:50. I found no guard the finder missed. Two of the three claims hold; the Unknown one shows no defect.

**1. The merge reads received (holds).**
- lovejoin.ts:8225 `const besides = [...(spent ? [spent.class] : []), ...(ties ?? []).map(madePrivate)];`
- lovejoin.ts:8230 `origin = spent || !plain ? (besides.length ? merged([own, ...besides]) : own) : undefined;`
- histories.ts:140 `REACH = ["session", "own", "received", "lovejoin", "unknown"]`, and originOfAll (:149-154) names the first one found.
- So `merged([unplacedBox(w), received:R])` is `box:w+received:R+unknown:w`, origin `received`.

Nothing changes that origin later:
- WebAssembly takes the origin as given (lib.rs:2153 `"received" => Origin::Received`).
- activity.ts classOf (:807-810) returns the stored class for a lovejoin-withdraw, which isn't in LEAVES_CHANGE (:800), and readClass keeps the origin.
- The copy rule (activity.ts:488-504) only matches a register already in the view, and the way back's register is fresh.

So the class gets build.rs:2509 Mint `Received => 1`, :2521 Fund `Received => 1`, and :2538 tier 0: tied with money others paid, and no longer a box.

How it's reached:
- Bring every box back now takes every box, with no someone-else filter (lovejoin.ts:7770-7772).
- It pays a stuck pool's box from the private balance (:7892).
- The payer order (:8132-8137) is boxes first, then no other account, then the smallest. WebAssembly skips UTxOs holding tokens (wasm lovejoin.rs:2969).

Run, case 1:
- Setup: a1 (25 ₳, Unknown), Bob's 20 ₳ received, and Mallory's 2 ₳ + LJTEST box in the token pool, under S1's register byte for byte. Pool parameters set so its boxes can't pay their own way back (coins_per_utxo_size 4800).
- The withdraw spent the box and Bob's UTxO. The way back was sealed `{"id":"box:<w>+received:b0…+unknown:<w>","origin":"received"}`.
- Peter's 50 ₳ then arrived. The next stealth mint spent the way back alone, not Peter's payment. The new Seedelf is tied in the open to S1, which is l2rank#1's harm.

This is no regression from 5447f7e5 for this box, which read received there whether merged or not. A plain boxFrom paid with received money has read received since call 36 too. But round three's rule 1 and its docs now say otherwise:
- architecture.md:152: "still a box to selection, which `Mint` and `Fund` take after money others paid".
- The unreleased policy entry (privacy-policy.md:93): "any other goes after money others paid you".
- Only privacy.md:169 has the exception. The fixer's "stuck-pool edge, accepted" (round3.json, R3-code l2rank#1) was the fixer's call, not the owner's.

**2. The payer order now prefers such a box (holds, new in round three).**
- lovejoin.ts:8132 `fromLovejoin` gives 0 to origin lovejoin or mixed. unplacedBox (histories.ts:80) has origin lovejoin.
- At 5447f7e5 this way back was receivedIn or unknownIn, so it got 1.
- Now it pays first, as "a box back from Lovejoin made, which ties no account" (:8124), tied by size with a box the wallet knows mixed.

Run, case 2:
- Mallory's d = 1 box in the 5 ₳ pool came back by Bring every box back now as W, `box:<w>+unknown:<w>`, about 4.7 ₳. A 9.7 ₳ mixed way back M was also in the private balance.
- Bring one back paid privately, for the user's own mixed token-pool box V, spent V and W, not M.
- V's way back is `box:<v>+box:<w>+unknown:<w>`: the user's mixed box is now tied in the open to the box that carried S1's register.
- At 5447f7e5, M would have paid.

**3. The Unknown claim shows no defect.** A box paid with Unknown money reads lovejoin (Mint 2). Rule 1 itself spells a box of unknown making as box plus unknown, origin lovejoin, and boxFrom merged with `unknown:<U>` read lovejoin before round three too.

**Why low.**
- A stranger's deposit costs only a fee, and a d = 1 copy makes the tie public.
- It then needs a pool whose boxes can't pay their own way back (or a privately paid Bring one back), plus the user's bring-back or a retired pool's run.
- Case 1 also needs no box that pays in the balance, a received payment as the smallest payer, and a later private mint or funding where the way back is the smallest rank-1 UTxO that pays alone.
- Case 2 also needs another box in the balance.
- No funds move. Settings' bringCost says the paying UTxO is tied to the box.
verdicts.fix_notes:
**1. withdrawOne (lovejoin.ts:8230): keep the way back a box.**
When the private balance paid and `own.origin` is `"lovejoin"` (boxFrom or unplacedBox), keep origin lovejoin where merged() names the merge received:
```ts
const all = besides.length ? merged([own, ...besides]) : own;
origin = spent || !plain ? (spent && own.origin === "lovejoin" && all.origin === "received" ? { ...all, origin: "lovejoin" } : all) : undefined;
```
- The sketch's "unknown" case can't happen: `own` always has a box part, which REACH puts ahead of unknown.
- A mixedBox paid with received money stays received (Mint 1), which is fine: only its payer knows it.
- Merges with session, own or change money are unchanged.
- No Rust change is needed: readClass and lib.rs keep a stored origin. settleWithdrawing (:8432) copies `w.origin`, so a resumed withdraw gets it too.
- Tested in the copy: case 1 passes, and 64 files (tests/lovejoin*, escape-hatch*, r3-*, b15*, histories*, coin-control*, maybe-sent, unlock-resend, write-ahead, settle-history*) pass: 1117 passed, 2 skipped.

**2. Payer order (lovejoin.ts:8132): a box of unknown making after the other boxes.**

Setting: preprod, or mainnet with Settings' Koios-only switch on, or with the data layer down, or a pool ours doesn't cover. A box someone else's mix moved since sits in the 5 ₳ pool, or in the retired classic pool. It has a due time, so no pool read asks about it (moreThanDue is false).

findings.title: The 1.9.1 open-entry backfill of `depositors` runs only inside sortOut. A Bring every box back run, the retired pools' run on a 1.7 profile, or a 1.9.1 withdraw settling first can close a released private Bootstrap's entry by count before any sortOut runs. That Bootstrap's own deposit boxes then come back as box+unknown, not box+session:n
findings.scenario:
Starting state, on a 1.9.1 profile:
- Private Bootstrap E belongs to session 4. Its record went 3 h after it ended, as 1.9.1 drops it.
- E's entry is still open, with 1 box at its deposit D. leaves = {D#0: "session.4"}. No `depositors` entry exists: 1.9.1 kept them for public accounts only.
- E was released, by Bring them all back, or on a 1.7 profile by retireOnce.
- A Bring every box back run asked before the update is still going.

After the update:
1. withdrawDueNow returns bringAllBackNow at once (7234-7235). bringAllBackNow never calls sortOut, so the backfill never runs.
2. The run takes box X first. X is someone else's mix output, a restore's box or another device's.
3. dropWithdrawing(gone) → countBack finds no open non-Bootstrap entry, so `released[0]` credits E. E is closed, and update drops it.
4. Next comes D#0. depositsNamed lacks D, and depositSessionOf finds no chain, no entry, no depositor and no answer. deposited is undefined and ownMixOf is false.
5. withdrawOne seals unplacedBox (box:<w>+unknown:<w>, lovejoin), tagged Back from Lovejoin and Unknown, Mint and Fund rank 2.

Rule 1(b) says it is box+session:4, which Mint ranks last. The next stealth mint with no mixed box or received money that pays alone takes it before change and money made private. The new Seedelf is then tied on chain to session 4's one-time account and its funding.

This is not a false mixed mark: D#0 sits in `leaves`, so the origins path is off, and mixedLeaves never holds it. The fixer's tests (r3-way-back-classes.test.ts:339-355) call status() first, so they always run the backfill.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 51e66221. I found no guard the finder missed, and three paths reproduce it.

**Where the backfill lives.** `depositors` is written in two places only, both inside sortOut's update:
- lovejoin.ts:6376-6379 writes it for chain records going now.
- lovejoin.ts:6383-6387 is the open-entry backfill: `for (const e of entries(s)) { if (!(e.bootstrap || e.seed) || s.chains.some((c) => c.id === e.id)) continue; const deposit = e.deposit ?? (e.session === undefined ? e.id : undefined); if (deposit) (s.depositors ??= {})[deposit] ??= whose(e.session, e.account); }`.

The read normalizer (8540-8545) only filters `depositors`. cuts() (6188-6213), ours() (3561-3602), reservedBoxes, bringAllBackNow's landed update and bringSays never write it.

**When sortOut runs.** It has three callers: status (6817), withdrawDueNow (7264) and withdrawNowNow (7520).
- status is reached only from the Lovejoin screen (ui/screens/Lovejoin.tsx:1828 → handlers.ts:525-526). Home and the worker's runs never call it; runs.ts:95 calls withdrawDue alone.

**Paths that close the entry before any sortOut.**
- withdrawDueNow 7232-7235: `await this.retireOnce(network); const asked = (await this.read(network)).bringing; if (asked && !asked.stopped) return this.bringAllBackNow(network, asked);`. bringAllBackNow (7706-7894) never calls sortOut.
- withdrawDueNow 7248: settleWithdrawing runs before sortOut at 7264.
- withdrawNowNow 7483: settleWithdrawing runs before sortOut at 7520.
- On a 1.7 profile, retireOnce (4553-4628) sets `e.released = true` on every Bootstrap in a retired pool and `s.bringing = { at: now, back: 0, retired: true }`. The very first run therefore goes to bringAllBackNow.

**How the entry closes.**
- Each withdraw ends in dropWithdrawing(..., gone=true) (8318, 8418), which calls countBack (8341).
- countBack 2618: `const released = bootstrap ? [] : openIn(s, p, true).filter((e) => e.released);`
- countBack 2622: `const target = unmixed ?? its ?? candidates.find((e) => outIn(e, p) > leftOf(s, e)) ?? candidates[0] ?? released[0];`
- So a box X that isn't held, in a pool with no open non-Bootstrap entry, credits the released Bootstrap E.
- update() then drops E: 8660 `schedule.mixes = (schedule.mixes ?? []).filter(open)`.

**How D#0 is then classed** (withdrawOne 8215-8222):
- depositSessionOf (2412-2421) finds no chain and no entry. 2416-2417 `const kept = s.depositors?.[b.txHash]; if (kept) return kept.session;` finds nothing either. There is no `origins` entry: D#0 is in `leaves`, so Koios is never asked.
- mixedBoxOf (2444-2449) is false, because recorded() is true through `leaves` and there is no `mixedLeaves`. ownMixOf is false.
- The result is `unplacedBox(built.txHash)`, i.e. box+unknown with origin lovejoin.
- `leaves[D#0] = "session.4"` is read only by originOf and madeSince, never by the class.

**Harm.** seedelf-core/src/build.rs:2512-2520, Purpose::Mint ranks Mixed 0, Received 1, Lovejoin 2, Unknown 3, Change 4, Own 5, Session 6. Rule 1(b)'s box+session:4 ranks last. The misclass ranks 2, ahead of change (4) and money made private (madePrivate's origin is "own", 5). Fund ranks Lovejoin 2 against Session 6.

**Reproduced in a copy.** Three cases fail on HEAD:
- a Bring every box back run asked before the update;
- X's withdraw maybe-sent at the update, settled first inside Bring one back;
- a 1.7 profile whose first run is retireOnce's.

The control, the same state with status() called first, passes. That matches the fixer's tests (r3-way-back-classes.test.ts:339-355), which call status() first.

With the backfill moved into update(), all 4 cases pass. Also 65 files matching tests/lovejoin*, bootstrap*, chain*, r2*, r3*, l3* pass (1047 tests, 2 skipped), and tsc --noEmit is clean.

**Why low.** It needs the state 1.9.1 (or 1.7) left behind: a private Bootstrap's record gone, its entry open, no depositor. It also needs E released, another box counted to E first, and the window between the update and the first sortOut. On this release's own state, the depositor is written in the same sortOut update that drops the record (6376-6379). The owner already accepts the same box+unknown outcome for entries that 1.9.1 closed before the update. No funds are at risk and no stranger can cause it.
verdicts.fix_notes:
**Fix (a few lines, nothing new kept).** Do the open-entry backfill in update() (lovejoin.ts:8642-8665), every write's path, after `entries(schedule);` (8648) and before `change(schedule);` (8649). Use the same shape sortOut uses:

```ts
const seen = this.deps.now();
for (const e of entries(schedule)) {
  if (!(e.bootstrap || e.seed) || schedule.chains.some((c) => c.id === e.id)) continue;
  const deposit = e.deposit ?? (e.session === undefined ? e.id : undefined);
  if (deposit) (schedule.depositors ??= {})[deposit] ??= e.session === undefined ? { account: e.account ?? 0, seen } : { session: e.session, seen };
}
```

Best extracted as a helper, e.g. keepOpenDepositors(s, now).

- **sortOut's copy.** sortOut's own loop (6380-6387) becomes redundant, since its write also passes through update(). Drop it or keep it; it's harmless either way.
- **Keep sortOut's chain-record write** (6376-6379) where it is: it depends on keep(c) as records go.
- **Pruning.** `??=` makes the loop idempotent. sortOut's prune (6388-6392) still ages a depositor out RECORD_KEEP_MS after the entry closes with no box listed at D. While the entry is open, the depositor is re-added on each write, as sortOut's loop does today.
- **Nothing else changes.** empty() is unaffected, since an open entry is already non-empty. Nothing is kept that round three doesn't already keep (private-session depositors are this release's), so no new privacy-policy entry is needed.
- **Close-time write: not recommended.** Writing the depositor in countBack when it closes an entry whose record is gone would need `now` threaded through, and would miss the other close paths.

**Tests.** Add the three cases below, none calling status():
1. `{due: [], chains: [], retired, mixes: [E released, 1 box at D], leaves: {D#0: "session.4"}, bringing: {at, back: 0}}`, with X (madeByAdaMix) listed before D, and withdrawDue.
2. Make X's withdraw maybe-sent (a 503 on submittx), strip `depositors`, set confirmations to 1, then withdrawNow(D), whose settle runs before its sortOut.
3. A 1.7 classic-pool state with no `retired` and E not yet released, X listed first, and withdrawDue, so retireOnce releases E and starts the bring run.

Each expects D's way back to be `box:<w>+session:4` with origin session; today it is `box:<w>+unknown:<w>` with origin lovejoin.

**Comments and record.** Rewrite the 6380-6382 comment to say the backfill runs on every write. Correct round three's "the class no longer depends on the count" note: it held only once a sortOut had run.

**Owner's alternative.** Accept it as part of 1.9.1's already-closed class, since the outcome is identical.

findings.title: The escape hatch's private payer now picks a box of unknown making first, with the boxes it knows. A stuck token box's way back can then spend a stranger's d = 1 box's way back
findings.line: 8132 (with shared/histories.ts 80; reached from 7871/7892 and from withdrawNowNow's paid "private"; docs/flows.md 526)
findings.scenario:
1. Mallory deposits a 5 ₳ box under Seedelf S1's register as found (d = 1).
2. Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run or Bring one back anyway brings it back without asking. withdrawOne seals W1 = box:W1+unknown:W1, origin lovejoin (unplacedBox).
3. Later a token pool's box B2 can't pay its own way back. Its question defaults to Pay from my private balance; Bring every box back now's stuck path does the same (`paid: "private"`). The worker orders the private balance's ADA-only UTxOs by `fromLovejoin`, then `another`, then smallest first.
4. W1's UTxO now sits in the first group beside every genuine way back. At about 4.7 ₳ it is often the smallest, so B2's withdraw spends it.
5. Anyone reading S1's name sees its register in the box W1 spent. B2's way back, and the fact that the token box was the user's, are now tied to S1, and Mallory learns it.

Round two kept W1 as received:<w>, in the second group after the boxes. 1.9.1 had it as a plain box, in the first group, so this restores 1.9.1's pick.

Other boxes of unknown making land in the same group:
- an unsure box after a restore, possibly the user's own public account's deposit, which `another` can't see;
- a 1.9.1-kept private Bootstrap deposit box read as (d) (l3time#2), which ties session n.

findings.title: l2docs#1's seedelf-data term runs the whole web wallet check on every data-layer Rust PR, for one regex the data layer's own job could run in seconds
findings.scenario:
A maintainer opens a PR that changes only seedelf-data/api/src/public/utxos.rs, an API fix or a hotfix while the API misbehaves.

Before round three, `covered` gave platform=false. Every web wallet job skipped, Web Wallet required went green at once, and data-layer.yml ran the data layer's own check.

Now `/^seedelf-data\/.*\.rs$/` gives platform=true, so all of these run: rust (`cargo test --workspace` of seedelf-platform), wasm, unit (both builds), e2e and store. That is about 13 minutes warm (#343's figures in the CI-speed memory: unit 11.5, e2e 11.7, store 9). main's ruleset requires Web Wallet required with no bypass, so the PR can't merge until the wallet's whole suite passes, e2e flakes included.

For this PR the run adds one thing: workflows.test.ts's docs#11 assertion that no include_str!/include_bytes! under seedelf-data names a .md file.

This is the data layer's ordinary PR: 30 of the 42 commits that touched seedelf-data's Rust touched nothing under seedelf-platform. It isn't B12's rare .hex PR, whose rarity was the reason for a covered term. A data-layer hotfix must land on main before data-layer-deploy.yml can ship it, so it now waits on the wallet's suite too.

The test-tools.sh term has B12's shape (5 commits ever touched the script) and is fine.

   - The fixer's round3.json "left" only records the cost ("about 13 minutes").
   - No lead message, OWNER line or DECISIONS entry picks the covered route for seedelf-data.
   - review2's verifier put the data-layer step first as its fix 2. Its test 2 did accept either shape (`if (walletRuns(rs)) return;`).
   - The CI-speed memory says: "put it in its own parallel job unless it truly needs another's output; say what it adds to wall time". This check needs no other job's output.

**What doesn't hold**

1. **The count.** Only 20 of the 42 commits that touched seedelf-data's Rust have no file under seedelf-platform. The finder's 30 counts commits whose own files the old filter skips.

2. **Commits aren't what CI runs on.**

Low: a CI cost on a PR shape that hasn't happened yet. It doesn't touch funds, privacy or wallet behaviour.

findings.title: The policy now says a box you bring back yourself is never asked about, but Bring one back now and a stuck pool's Bring one back ask Koios what made it
findings.scenario:
This applies wherever Koios answers: preprod, or mainnet with Read Cardano through Koios only, the data layer down, or a later pool of the same box value. A box someone else's mix moved since the wallet's own chain left it sits in one of the current pools. No record names it and no answer is kept. backOrder puts exactly such a box first.

The user presses Bring one back now on that pool's page, or Bring one back in a pool whose boxes can't pay their own way back (the escape hatch, paid from the private balance by default). withdrawNowNow puts the boxes ranked ahead of the first known one into `force`. sortOut, found and lookUp then send Koios tx_info for those boxes' transactions, which tells Koios, from the user's IP, which boxes are theirs.

The policy says the opposite in three places:

The finding holds on HEAD (51e66221). I found no guard the finder missed.

The path a stranger's deposit takes:

That reaches `return ctx.lovejoin.status(ctx.network);` (handlers.ts:526), then status's sortOut (lovejoin.ts:6817), then `const found = await this.found(network, owned, listed, before, force, pools, old);` (6291).

  - 6475: `const unknown = owned.filter((b) => !known(b) && !kept[b.txHash]);`. Mallory's box has no chain record and no kept origin, so it is unknown.
  - 6480: `return moreThanDue(s, inPool(owned, p), inPool(listed, p), p, old.has(p)) ? theirs : theirs.filter(...)`
  - 6484: `const ask = unknown.filter((b) => holding.has(b.txHash) || forced.has(ref(b)));`
  - 6486: `const origins = await this.lookUp(network, ask, holding);`
- moreThanDue (2182): `return back > dueIn(s, p).length - theirDue;`. Her box isn't in `held`: it has no origin yet, so depositsOf skips it. It counts in `back` with no due time, so the check is true for that pool.
- So every unrecorded box in that pool is asked about in one request: her deposit, and every box of the wallet's that other people's mixes moved. In the steady state those moved boxes are never asked about.
- lookUp sends a box to Koios when its pool isn't covered by our server's listing: `const covered = ...` and `const koios = new Set(ask.filter((b) => !covered(poolOf(b)))...)` (6531-6532). The request is `koiosAlone()` then `koios.txSpends(...)`, which is tx_info (6698, 6702).

- rejudge (6626) touches only origins already kept.
- recorded() and knownOf() (2080, 2091) know only the wallet's own chains and leaves.
- On mainnet with our server answering, `covered` is true and nobody is asked, as the policy already says. So the ask reaches Koios on preprod, with Koios-only on, while ours is down, or for a later pool of the same box value.

After the ask, her box is held as someone else's deposit. It is never due, so it never comes back by itself, and Mix my boxes again from the private balance leaves it out. So the ask happens at none of the policy's three times:
- privacy-policy.md:28: "after a restore, before mixing it again, and before it comes back by itself from one of Lovejoin's current pools".
- privacy-policy.md:44: "before mixing it again or before it comes back by itself ..., and after a restore about all such boxes together". The grouping is tied to a restore only, but here a wallet that was never restored groups its moved boxes with her box.
- privacy-policy.md:93: the 18 November entry's last sentence repeats the same list as the corrected one.

- A wallet in its steady state asks nothing at the page's read.
- After her deposit, the next page read asks tx_info once, naming [B, C, M] together.
- Her box ends up in someoneElse, with no new due time and no giveme.my call.

Who can cause it:
- A stranger, at will. Each trigger costs her 5 ₳ plus the fee, and the box becomes the victim's.
- A user with the phrase on two devices. That case reads as "after a restore" only if the restore is taken loosely.

Why low: no funds move, and the sources are trusted. The policy already says Koios learns which boxes are yours. Only this time, and the grouping that comes with it, are missing.

findings.title: Change from a Make public that 1.9.1 sent to the user's own account now reads as Change and goes before money made private, though privacy.md and flows.md say such change carries that account's tag and goes with its money or after it
findings.scenario:
With 1.9.1, Alice received Bob's 50 ₳ (received:R) and made 20 ₳ public to her own account 2. 1.9.1 sealed that Make public's 30 ₳ change C as received:R, with no account part. She updates. Her private balance now holds C and 100 ₳ she made private from account 1 (public:0). She creates a Seedelf from the private balance.

classOf reads the 1.9.1 entry through spendLeft. The kept history names no account, so it gets change:S and origin change. Mint ranks Change 4 and Own 5, so the mint spends C. On chain, C is the change of the transaction that paid account 2. Anyone can tie the new Seedelf to account 2, and Bob can tie it to his payment. The UTxOs screen tags C "Change, Received", not "Made private (account 2)".

The docs say otherwise:
- privacy.md:109: change "tied to one of your accounts … (what a Make public to the account left …) goes with that money, or after it".
- privacy.md:176 and flows.md:134: the account tag "also marks what a Make public to that account left".
- privacy.md:172: old change "gets its spend's tie", where the tie of a Make public to one of your own accounts is "to that account".

R3-code named this residue ("can't be told apart and reads as change"), and no doc says it. Rule 2 itself ("never where the class names public:<n>") is followed exactly. The gap is the docs' general claim.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 51e66221. I found no guard that catches it, and the gap is a little wider than the finding says.

**How 1.9.1 kept the change.**
- `web-wallet/1.9.1` withdraw.ts:147 has `origin: changeHistory(seen, p.inputs)`, and script-spend.ts:171-172 has `return merged(inputs.map((i) => classOf(classes, i)))`. So only the inputs' history was kept, with no part for the account that was paid.
- 1.9.1's activity.ts sent() (:334-374) stores `readClass(s.origin)`. Its withdraw entry keeps the payee only as `detail: shortHex(String(p.address))`, which is the first 12 characters + "…" + the last 6, for the first payee only, with `more` counting the rest.

**What HEAD does.**
- HEAD adds the payee's account only when it builds a Make public: withdraw.ts:152-155 `tiedBy` returns `madePrivate(d.ownAccount)`, and :165 has `origin: merged([changeHistory(seen, p.inputs), ...tiedBy(p)])`.
- Reading a 1.9.1 entry:
  - activity.ts:800 has `LEAVES_CHANGE = new Set(["transfer", "withdraw", "mint", "remove", "lovejoin-launch"])`.
  - activity.ts:810 has `if (stored) return LEAVES_CHANGE.has(entry.kind) ? spendLeft(stored, entry.txHash) : stored;`.
  - histories.ts:187-191 has `if (all.some(left)) return merged([kept]); if (all.some((p) => accountIn(p) !== undefined)) return kept; return merged([kept, leftBy(txHash)]);`.
  - originOfAll (:149-154) then gives origin "change".
- Paid from received money, a box or Unknown, the change reads `{id: "change:S+received:R", origin: "change"}`.
- Paid from money made private (public:0), :190 returns public:0 unchanged. The tag then names the account the money came from, not the account that was paid.

**No guard.**
- classOf reads only `origin`, `kind` and `txHash`.
- classes() (activity.ts:473-506) rewrites only Received copies of a register.
- There is no history migration: sw.ts:334 onInstalled runs only `applyKept`.
- Utxos.tsx:50 tags straight from `historyTags(u.history, accounts)`.

**How selection ranks it.**
- build.rs Purpose::Mint has `Change => 4, Own => 5`, and Fund has the same two ranks.
- Step 1 sorts by (last, rank, lovelace) (`one_more` :2752, `ranked` :2857).

**What the docs say.** All of these lines are from round three (blame: 211c65c2 and b5c28f1e):
- privacy.md:109: such change "goes with that money, or after it".
- privacy.md:172: old change "gets its spend's tie", and for a Make public to your own account that tie is "to that account".
- privacy.md:176 and flows.md:134: the account tag "also marks what a Make public to that account left".
- keys-and-accounts.md:151: tags it with "the account that payment ties it to".
- The finder missed two more:
  - architecture.md:151: old change gets `change:<tx>` "but where that history names a public account, as a Make public's to one of the user's own accounts does". That is false for what 1.9.1 kept.
  - The comment on histories.ts:183-184 says the same.

round3.json l2time#2 "left" names this leftover case, and no doc mentions it. Before round three, 5447f7e5 activity.ts:794 had `if (stored) return stored;`: the same change read as Received, Mint rank 1. Round three narrowed the code's gap, but its docs claim the whole.

**Test results.** I ran a Vitest test on a copy of the tree, with the WebAssembly package built from HEAD (r3-change-classes passes 23/23 with it).
- Control, passes: a Make public to account 2 sent from HEAD reads `public:1+received:R0` with origin own, tagged `["Made private (account 2)","Received"]`. A stealth mint then takes the smaller 10 ₳ made private from account 1.
- The 1.9.1 version, fails: origin is "change" and the tags are `["Change","Received"]`. The mint takes that change (`5757…#1`) before the 10 ₳ from account 1.
- Also fails: a 1.9.1 Make public to account 2 from account 1's money is tagged `["Made private (account 1)"]` only, with no account 2.
- With the finding's own amounts (change 30 ₳, 100 ₳ made private), the docs' rule would pick the same change, because ranks are equal and the smaller goes first. There, only the tag and the stated reason differ. The pick itself differs only when the money made private is the smaller of the two.

**Why low.** By the rubric's letter this is a claim wider than the code, which is medium. But it only touches entries an earlier version kept. Either pick ties the new Seedelf to one of the user's own public accounts: account 2 plus Bob's payment, or account 1. So it adds no new kind of link.

**Who it affects.** Someone who updated from 1.9.1 (or earlier) and, with that version, made public to one of their own accounts while still holding its change. The tag gap applies for any inputs. The ranking gap applies when the inputs were received money, a box or Unknown money, and also when that Make public paid a stranger too: the docs put such change after money made private (rank 6), but it reads as rank 4.

- privacy.md:460: "Bring one back now's choice of box, may still ask Koios what made a box there".

findings.title: A box of unknown making is now the private balance's first pick to pay a stuck box's way back, so a planted d = 1 box's way back spreads S1's tie to the next box
findings.scenario:
1. Mallory deposits a 5 ₳ box under Seedelf S1's register as found (d = 1).
2. The user brings it back with Bring every box back now or Bring one back anyway. Its way back W is `box:W+unknown:W`, origin lovejoin: l2rank#1's fix, which is right for the stealth mint.
3. Later the user brings back a box B from a token pool whose boxes can't pay their own way back. The default payer is the private balance, and Bring every box back now pays that way too (:7892).
4. withdrawOne's payer order puts first every UTxO whose origin is lovejoin or mixed ("a box back from Lovejoin made, which ties no account"), so W pays when it's the smallest such.
5. B's way back spends W. Anyone who reads S1's name can now tie B's way back, and the private UTxO it makes, to S1.

In round two, W was `received:W` (or `unknown:W` for an unsure box), and this order put it after the boxes. The same now goes for the user's own deposits the wallet can't place: a 1.9.1 blind deposit answer, or another device's session past the book's indices. Spent first here, they tie the next way back to that session's funding.

This is where rule 1's origin meets call 36's payer order.
findings.who: A stranger (a ~5 ₳ deposit, which the user keeps), plus the user's own bring-backs. For the user's unplaced deposits, nobody.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 51e66221. I traced it end to end and found no guard the finder missed. A test fails on HEAD and passes with the fix.

1. A box no record places comes back as `box:W+unknown:W` with origin "lovejoin". withdrawOne classes it at lovejoin.ts:8215-8222. It is not mixed (`mixedBoxOf`), not a session's, not deposited by the user, and not the user's own mix, so it gets `unplacedBox(built.txHash)`. histories.ts:80 builds that as `merged([boxFrom, unknownIn])`. `originOfAll` (histories.ts:149) walks REACH (`["session","own","received","lovejoin","unknown"]`, :140), so the origin is "lovejoin". Because the class is not a plain box (lovejoin.ts:8229-8230), it is written to the history.
2. The class survives the read back unchanged.

   - activity.ts:485: `classOfRow` keeps any origin that isn't unknown.
   - script-spend.ts:277 drops only the bare id "unknown".
   - No filter: coin-control.ts:290 drops only rows the user locked, and readContract (script-spend.ts:220-247) drops only reserved rows.
3. The payer order puts it first. lovejoin.ts:8132 `const fromLovejoin = (u) => (["lovejoin","mixed"].includes(classes[outpoint(u)]?.origin ?? "") ? 0 : 1)`. Then :8135 `another` (0 for W, which has no public:<n> part), then the smallest (:8136-8138). WebAssembly spends the first owned, ADA-only UTxO that pays, in that order (wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:2951-3010).
4. The private balance is the default payer.
   - The escape hatch is shown only for a stuck pool (Lovejoin.tsx:3675-3687). Its PayerButtons put "Pay from my private balance" first (:1166-1172).
   - Bring every box back now pays a stuck pool's boxes privately (lovejoin.ts:7871, :7892).
   - W cannot pay in the same run that makes it: readContract reads Koios, and W isn't listed until it lands. So the scenario needs a later run or press, as the finder's "Later" says.
5. Round two classed these boxes apart. At 5447f7e5:lovejoin.ts:8166-8171 such a box was `receivedIn` or `unknownIn`, so `fromLovejoin` gave 1.
6. HEAD contradicts the approved design.
   - e1a#1 (4): "its box:<tx> class ranks after received money, so it ties no more than a payment from the planter would".
   - Rule 1: "after money others paid". Core ranks Lovejoin after Received for Mint and Fund, and last for Pay (build.rs:2494-2528).
   - Here a d = 1 payment from the planter becomes Unknown (activity.ts:487-507) and ranks second. The planter's box now ranks ahead of her payment.
   - privacy.md:432 ("One back from Lovejoin goes first, since it ties no account") and flows.md:526 give a reason that is false for this class.
7. Not a regression against the shipped 1.9.1. At f265d178:lovejoin.ts:7602 and :7665, every way back the private balance didn't pay was read as `box:<tx>` (origin lovejoin) and ranked first. Round two's classes moved it out as a side effect, and round three moved it back.

- Mallory's d = 1 box is brought back anyway: W ≈ 4.8 ₳, class unplaced.
- A box of the wallet's in the classic pool that a mix made is brought back: M ≈ 9.8 ₳, class mixed.
- A stuck token pool box is then brought back, paid privately. HEAD spends W, in the default build and with VITE_ENABLE_MAINNET=false. With the fix it spends M.
- With the fix, the neighbouring suites pass: lovejoin-merged-review, r3-way-back-classes, lovejoin-someone-else, escape-hatch-unknown-ahead and escape-hatch-reserved, 70 tests in all.

findings.title: Every pull request that changes only the data layer's Rust now waits on the web wallet's whole required check
findings.scenario:
l2docs#1 added `/^seedelf-data\/.*\.rs$/` to `covered`. A PR that touches only seedelf-data's Rust now sets platform=true and runs all five web-wallet jobs: Rust, WebAssembly, unit, e2e and store package (about 13 minutes, R3-misc says). That's on top of data-layer.yml.

main's ruleset requires the Web Wallet required job, so every such PR's merge waits for that suite. Before, the suite was skipped and the job went green at once.

All the suite checks for that PR is one rule: no seedelf-data .rs file may include_str! or include_bytes! a .md file. The test-tools.sh half costs little, since such a PR is rare.
findings.who: Nobody: maintainers' ordinary data-layer PRs.
findings.evidence:
web-wallet.yml:75 `covered='… || /^seedelf-verification\/test-tools\.sh$/ || /^seedelf-data\/.*\.rs$/ || …'`.
round3.json R3-misc left: "a pull request that changes only seedelf-data's Rust now also runs the web wallet's whole check (about 13 minutes)".
The l2docs#1 fix list offered a cheaper step in data-layer.yml.
The owner's standing note that CI speed matters.
findings.fix: Keep test-tools.sh in `covered`. Drop the seedelf-data pattern, and give data-layer.yml its own step: `! grep -rnE 'include_(str|bytes)!\(\s*"[^"]*\.md"' --include='*.rs' seedelf-data`. Point workflows.test.ts's docs#11 comment at that step. Or keep it as is, and say the cost in the covered comment.
findings.owner_question: Should a data-layer-only Rust PR run the web wallet's full suite (about 13 minutes on the required check), or get a one-line grep in data-layer.yml instead?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. I traced it on HEAD 51e66221 and found no guard the finder missed. Its own fix, as written, doesn't work (point 7).

1. **The new term.** web-wallet.yml:75 now includes `/^seedelf-data\/.*\.rs$/`. git blame puts it in 9d512644, round three's l2docs#1. The `changes` step (:76) sets platform=true when this awk program exits 0. I ran the exact program from main, 5447f7e5 and HEAD on single paths:
   - seedelf-data/api/src/main.rs, api/src/lovejoin/standard.rs and api/tests/live_public.rs: skipped on main and on 5447f7e5, run on HEAD.
   - seedelf-data/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and README.md: skipped on all three.

2. **The required check waits on all five jobs.** Each job has `if: needs.changes.outputs.platform == 'true'` (:85, :122, :170, :218, :260). `required` (:305-320) needs all of them. Once platform=true it passes only on `success success success success success` (:318), so it reports after the slowest job: about 13 minutes (R3-misc's own "left"; the memory has #343's run at 13.2 min). main's ruleset requires this check with no bypass (:298-300, development.md:13). data-layer.yml starts too (`seedelf-data/**`, :8) and runs alongside. It can't be the required check, because its path filter means it doesn't run on every PR.

3. **What the suite checks for such a PR: one rule.** In seedelf-platform, every mention of seedelf-data is a comment except workflows.test.ts:
   - :440-463 is docs#11's rule: no seedelf-data .rs file includes a .md file.
   - :533-536 is l2docs#1's test, which only checks that each .rs file triggers the check. Given the `.*\.rs$` term, that always passes.
   - No Rust test, wasm test, e2e or store step reads seedelf-data.

4. **No guard.** There's no paths-ignore and no exemption for a data-only file list. A one-file PR has rows=1=CHANGED, so awk alone decides.

5. **Where it's wider than the code shows:**
   - (a) "Ordinary" data-layer PRs: none has happened yet. Of 247 PRs merged into main, 15 touched seedelf-data .rs files, and all 15 also touched seedelf-platform code or a workflow, so none would have paid this cost (checked with GNU grep and HEAD's awk minus the term). The real case is a future data-only fix, such as an API hotfix. data-layer-deploy.yml builds main alone (:5, :9), so that fix must merge first.
   - (b) "On top of data-layer.yml": the two run side by side. The extra wait beyond data-layer.yml's own run is about 13 minutes minus its run time. I couldn't measure that offline. data-layer.yml has no push trigger, so it has no main cache.
   - (c) The aside that the test-tools.sh term costs little because such PRs are rare isn't borne out. 3 of the 6 merged PRs that touched seedelf-verification's .sh or .py tools touched nothing else covered: #368, #372 and #381. #372 and #381 changed check.sh, which test-tools.sh now tests, so that wait probably lands more often than this one. That's for the owner. This finding is about the data half.

6. Severity is low: a CI wait in an edge case, no effect on the wallet, funds or privacy. It does go against the CI-speed memory ("code PRs' check must be fast"; "say what it adds to wall time"). The `covered` comment (:40-46) doesn't state this cost.

7. **The finding's fix fails three ways as written.** I tested each in a copy:
   - **Wrong folder.** data-layer.yml's `check` job runs in seedelf-data/ (defaults, :37-39), so `grep … seedelf-data` fails with "No such file or directory" (exit 2). `!` turns that into 0, so the step passes on every crate, even one that includes Markdown.
   - **YAML eats the `!`.** On one line as a plain scalar (`run: ! grep …`), YAML reads `! ` as a tag. Ruby's YAML gives `grep -rnE … seedelf-data`, with the `!` gone. That command exits 2, so every data-layer PR would go red.
   - **Wrapped includes are missed.** A line-by-line grep misses an include whose path is on the next line, and rustfmt wraps 5 of the crate's 10 includes that way: datum.rs:587, standard.rs:103 and :611, templates.rs:400, live_public.rs:848.
verdicts.fix_notes:
I checked all of this in a copy: workflows.test.ts gives 17 passed, and tsc is clean. If the owner keeps the term instead, add one line to web-wallet.yml's covered comment (:40-46): a PR that changes only seedelf-data's Rust waits about 13 minutes on Web Wallet required, for docs#11's one rule. Then skip the rest.

1. **web-wallet.yml.**
   - :75: drop ` || /^seedelf-data\/.*\.rs$/`. Keep the test-tools.sh term, though point 5(c) of the evidence is a reason to ask the owner about it too.
   - :42-43: drop "and the data layer's Rust".
   - :40-41: add to the rule that a check reading outside seedelf-platform/ may instead be made by a workflow its own PRs start, naming data-layer.yml's "No Markdown included".

2. **data-layer.yml.** Add this step to `check`. It needs no toolchain, so it can go first for a fast failure, or before "The deploy script". Write it as a block, never `run: ! grep …` on one line.

findings.title: A spared mark set because another tab waited for the unlock on a non-connect call is never cleared by the unlock, so a later page leaving mid-enable lands a decline nobody owed
findings.scenario:
1. A connected site's tab B calls signTx while the wallet is locked: an unlock wait with enable false.
2. The same site's tab A calls enable(), which waits for the unlock too.
3. A reloads. gone(A) finds B in `unlocking`, so sharedBeyond is true, and it records `spared` for the site.
4. The user unlocks. Line 790 resolves and drops every unlock waiter but leaves `spared`. Only an enable()'s unlock wait, a connect question, refuseFor, the site's last enabling page ending, or connectorOff clears it.
5. The first later enable() of that site normally finishes and clears the mark. If its page leaves before it finishes instead (a tab closed or reloaded during its reads), gone() calls sparedNoMore, which calls refuseFor.
6. For the connected site, refusing then turns its getUtxos and signTx calls away as NOT_CONNECTED (:1641) for the 10 s back-off, though the user answered the unlock.

It's rare and costs only a nuisance. It's where sign#3's "or waits for the unlock itself" meets l2sign#1's debt.
findings.who: A connected site with two tabs, plus ordinary timing.
findings.evidence:
dapp.ts:954 `else this.spared.set(session.origin, { title: session.title, ...(network ? { network } : {}) });`
dapp.ts:972 `this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin)` (any method).
dapp.ts:790 `for (const u of this.unlocking.splice(0)) u.resolve();` (no clear).
dapp.ts:1658 `if (enable) this.spared.delete(origin);`
dapp.ts:987 `this.refuseFor(origin, spared.title, spared.network);`
findings.fix:
Clear `spared` for each origin whose unlock waiters line 790 resolves, since the unlock window was answered. Or set `spared` only when the sparing page is an enable() in `enabling`.

Test (dapp-gone): with the wallet locked, tab B waits on signTx and tab A on enable(). gone(A), then unlock. A third page's enable() is held at its sealed read, then gone(third). declined() must stay [] and B's next call must not be refused.

verdicts.evidence:
The defect holds, but not by the finder's steps. I traced it on HEAD 51e66221 and ran tests in a copy. The fixes tree is clean and the copy is deleted.

**The finder's literal steps don't reproduce. Here is the guard they missed.**
- In their scenario B's call is a signTx, so it isn't counted in `enabling`. A is the site's only page there.
- gone(A) does set the mark (dapp.ts:954, via the unlocking clause at :972). It then rejects A's unlock wait, so A's call ends at once.
- call()'s finally (:606 `if (method === "enable") this.countEnabling(session, -1);`) then empties the site's `enabling`, and countEnabling clears the mark (:618-621 `this.enabling.delete(session.origin); ... this.spared.delete(session.origin);`).
- So by step 4 there is no mark left. Test 1 below passes on HEAD and checks this directly.
- The finder's own test couldn't fail anyway. `declined()` leaves connected sites out (:1316 `!connected.has(origin)`). And an unlocked connected site's calls never check the refusal: enable() returns at :1169-1173, before :1198, and other methods don't look at it.

**What does hold: the mark outlives the unlock whenever no enable() ends to clear it.**
- **V1: A's unlock wait is a signTx, signData or submitTx.** gone(A) marks the site because B waits (:972, :954). A's call isn't an enable(), so countEnabling never runs. :790 `for (const u of this.unlocking.splice(0)) u.resolve();` resolves B and leaves the mark. A signature's decline doesn't clear it either: answer() calls refuseFor only for a connect (:752). Any later enable() of the site whose page leaves before it finishes then lands the decline: gone() → sparedNoMore (:945) → refuseFor (:987). This works even an hour later (test 3).
- **V2: A's enable() leaves while another page's enable() (C) already waits for the unlock.** C's :1658 clear ran before the mark existed, so the mark stays through the unlock. If C's page leaves between the unlock and its connect question, the decline lands, though the unlock window A left was answered.
- **What it costs:**
  - A connected site (ordinary V1) is almost unaffected. A 10 s refusal is recorded but not listed. If the wallet is locked again within those 10 s, its signatures are refused NOT_CONNECTED at :1641 instead of opening the unlock window. getUtxos is refused at :635 while locked anyway, so the finder's getUtxos claim is wrong. A genuine decline within 10 minutes also starts at 60 s instead of 10 s.
  - A site that isn't connected (V1 through an API object kept after Disconnect, or V2) is listed as declined, with A's title. Its next enable() hears "The user declined this site just now. It can ask again in 10 s."
  - It's rare. The next enable() of the site clears the mark when it finishes, reaches its unlock wait (:1658) or asks (:1710), so its page must leave within those few milliseconds.
- **Policy reading:** privacy-policy.md:29 and :93 spare the site only "unless another of its pages is asking to connect too". By those words, A's leaving in V1 was owed a decline at once. Either way, a decline landing when some later, unrelated page leaves fits neither the policy nor architecture.md:563 ("If that page leaves too before it asks").

**Where two fixes meet:** the finder's first sketch, clearing every mark at :790, breaks l2sign#1. A connect question can keep waiting while the wallet locks (dapp-approvals-locked.test.ts). If its page leaves while another page's enable() waits for the unlock, and that page leaves after the unlock before asking, l2sign#1's decline is still owed. Test 5 passes on HEAD and fails with the simple sketch.
